extracted.intended_audience: Reuters journalists and editorial staff (text, TV, picture, online) and their managers
extracted.subtask_description: Company-wide editorial and ethical guidelines for Reuters journalists across text, television, picture and online services, covering accuracy, sourcing, independence, conflicts of interest, use of AI, visual standards, and professional conduct. Intended to govern everyday reporting, special cases (e.g., anonymous sources, market rumours), and outside activities and appearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Trust Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the Trust Principles in all activities related to Reuters News.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust Principles underpin Reuters' independence, accuracy and freedom from bias and should guide all journalistic decisions and conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold accuracy sacrosanct
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy is at the heart of what we do. It is our job to get it first but it is above all our job to get it right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy, as well as balance, always takes precedence over speed. Before pushing the button, think how you would withstand a challenge or denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek fair comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek fair comment in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give subjects the opportunity to put their side; avoid portraying allegations as fact and avoid language that implies editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct errors transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters is transparent about errors. We rectify them promptly, clearly and comprehensively, whether in a story, a caption, a graphic or a script.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections should be prompt and comprehensive; be open about mistakes to protect reputation and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strive for balance and freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive for balance and freedom from bias in stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Park nationality and politics at the door; reflect all sides of an issue and be mindful of word choice that may suggest bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose conflicts of interest to a manager
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose potential or actual conflicts of interest to a manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you think there is potential for conflict in any activity, raise it with your manager; failure to disclose can lead to disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid injecting unattributed opinion in news
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid injecting unattributed opinion in a news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not express opinions in news stories; opinion belongs in clearly labeled opinion pieces and attributed quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not fabricate or plagiarise
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not fabricate or plagiarise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabrication or plagiarism damages reputation and may lead to disciplinary measures including dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not alter visual material beyond normal editorial preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not alter still images or video footage beyond the methods normally used to prepare content for editorial use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visuals must reflect reality; altering images beyond standard editing can constitute fabrication and cause serious reputational damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: No payment for information or trading on privileged information
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not pay for information or accept a bribe or trade on privileged information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taking or offering payments for stories is a grave breach of ethics and may be grounds for immediate dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy: reflect reality and avoid hype
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy means that our images and stories must reflect reality; avoid hype or sensationalism that skews reality or misleads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stop to think about word choice (e.g., 'flood' vs. small number) and visual decisions; consider harm and necessity; senior editor decisions may be required for graphic content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections: transparent rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: Rectify errors promptly, clearly and comprehensively in stories, captions, graphics or scripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency in corrections preserves credibility; correct factual errors and be explicit about what was wrong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing: honesty and credibility of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy entails honesty in sourcing. A Reuters journalist or camera is generally the best source on a witnessed event; named sources are preferable to unnamed sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use named sources where possible; press sources to go on the record; unnamed sources used only when necessary and with editorial responsibility for accuracy; single anonymous-source stories require special authorization; protect confidentiality but be prepared to disclose source to supervisor on legitimate editorial grounds; cross-check information; seek two or more sources where possible; weigh track record, position and motive of unnamed sources; talk to sources on all sides; be explicit about what you don’t know; when initiative reporting, try to disprove as well as prove the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing practices and tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical guidance: take notes, record interviews where allowed, make ground rules clear, give context about sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record interviews where permitted; provide as much context and detail as possible about sources to authenticate information; be wary of imposters; communications can be interfered with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single anonymous source policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters will publish news from a single, anonymous source only in exceptional cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-source stories must be credible, from a trusted source with direct knowledge and are subject to a special authorisation procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes are sacrosanct
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes must never be altered other than to delete a redundant word or clause and then only if the deletion does not alter the sense of the quote in any way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure quotes are representative and provide context (body language); correct minor grammatical errors may be valid but avoid rewording entire phrases; consult senior journalist if unsure; translate idiomatically and preserve tone; when original-language retranslation is suspect, prefer fewer quotes and more reported speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datelines and bylines accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Datelines and bylines must accurately reflect presence on the ground; byline should show the writer was at the dateline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only use datelines where staff/freelancers are on the spot; contributors should be credited in an additional-reporting line with name and location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution for material not ours
rubrics_metrics.description: Properly attribute material that is not ours in stories, photographs or moving images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific in attribution (e.g., 'Greenpeace Video' or 'U.S. Army Photo'); labeling as 'handout' is insufficient and may raise plagiarism concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting rumours cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Report facts, not rumours; differentiate between fact and rumour and verify or knock down rumours affecting markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptional circumstances may require moving a story before full verification if markets are moving rapidly; attempt to verify or debunk rumours promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic images and obscenities: publish only when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic or obscene material should not be published gratuitously or to titillate; there must be a valid news reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually requires senior editor decision; consider whether material is necessary for understanding; be mindful of different market thresholds; packaged videos must carry 'Warning: Graphic Content' and RAW videos needs warnings in scripts and slates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence: avoid conflicts and perceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence is essential; avoid conflicts of interest or situations that could create a perception of conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt about potential conflicts in activities, raise with manager; independence extends to personal investments, outside work, gifts, travel, and editorial-commercial separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal investments prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not allow investments held by you or your immediate family to influence your Reuters work; do not report on or edit stories about entities in which you or family have an interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not trade in securities that would create reality or appearance of conflict; follow the Thomson Reuters Code of Conduct on personal investments and material nonpublic information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring financial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare financial interests and adhere to the Thomson Reuters Code of Conduct on investments and access to nonpublic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to adhere to these standards is subject to disciplinary procedures in the relevant location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work outside Reuters requires permission
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not engage in paid work outside Reuters unless your manager has given permission in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission is routinely granted if activities do not affect Reuters; NewsGuild US members only need permission for second jobs if they could be considered in competition with Reuters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking back with sources: no vetting by sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters does not submit stories, scripts or images to sources to vet before publication as this breaches independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may check back to verify a quote or fact but must ensure sources are not given opportunity to retract or materially alter information; resist requests to approve quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts and entertainment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept payment, gift, service or benefit offered by a news source or contact; consider cultural traditions and nominal gifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept only nominal-value traditional gifts; decline gifts of more than nominal value or surrender to manager; hospitality may be accepted if newsworthy and within reason; never accept 'junkets'; consult manager when unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and accommodation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard position is that we pay our own way and make our own travel arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If impractical and access is restricted, consult manager; permission normally given if story warrants coverage; reimburse relevant entity where possible; exceptional circumstances require manager permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bribes and inducements prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Under no circumstances should we take or offer payment (cash or in kind) for a news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such action is a grave breach of ethics and grounds for dismissal; Reuters does not permit facilitation payments; be aware of local legal restrictions when offering gifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence within Reuters (editorial-commercial separation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not write stories, take pictures or film events to help clinch a sales contract or alter coverage to suit Reuters' or Thomson Reuters' commercial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply sound news judgment; examine complaints about balance or accuracy raised by commercial colleagues; editorial independence is protected by Trust Principles and Board structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering competitions and awards rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees may submit Reuters work for awards only under strict conditions and with manager approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only to contests judged by journalists and with manager approval; submissions to contests not judged by journalists require senior approval; do not produce Reuters work primarily for awards; unsolicited awards and jury invitations need approval; avoid contests that could influence impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity and professional conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the highest ethical standards and the Trust Principles; exhibit personal integrity at all times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept responsibilities, adhere to acceptable professional standards, respect local laws and cultures while operating abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying ourselves as journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters journalists do not obtain news by deception and should identify themselves as Reuters journalists if directly questioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pass yourself off as something other than a journalist, except possible limited cases where an assumption may be allowed in the interests of newsgathering—apply common sense and consult Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting from the Internet
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the same standards of sourcing, identification and verification to reporting online as to other forms of newsgathering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take same precautions online; do not use unsourced material that you cannot verify; verify origin of online content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider trading prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters forbids staff to participate in insider trading and/or tipping information that could impact share prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat information obtained at work as non-public; examples of material information include contemplated mergers, bankruptcies, forecasts, changes in management; insider trading and tipping are criminal offences in many countries and carry heavy penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with sources: cultivate professionally and maintain detachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources must be cultivated professionally; maintain detachment and avoid relationships that compromise impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid spending excessive leisure time with sources; if in doubt, seek guidance; disclose romantic or family attachments with news sources to manager; do not report on or quote family members where it creates perception of favouritism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with customers: maintain editorial-commercial separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat customers (who may be news sources) with professional behaviours required of journalists and keep clear separation between editorial and commercial functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not negotiate sales contracts with clients; discuss news issues only in a clearly editorial context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with people in stories: sensitivity and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat victims with sensitivity, avoid needless pain and offence, seek clear accounts, avoid sensationalism, be wary of spin and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show integrity, impartiality, persistence, accountability and humility when covering people so stories can be defended to sources and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Compete vigorously but avoid improper or illegal collection and sharing of information with competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute competitors' exclusives; do not 'do deals' or trade material; cooperate when justified to reduce risk to life or when access is restricted; cooperate on staff safety and legitimate mutual interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate complaints promptly and properly when accuracy, balance or ethics are questioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge uninvestigable complaints at once and follow up quickly; handle complaints at senior level and escalate to Ethics and Standards where needed; respond with constructive attitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with the authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer any requests for unpublished Reuters content or journalists' notes from authorities to a senior editor and editorial legal team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between published and unpublished material; do not voluntarily hand over unpublished material; consider lawful challenges to subpoenas/orders to protect staff safety and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with each other: teamwork and safe workplace
rubrics_metrics.description: Teamwork across disciplines is required; staff should be able to raise standards and ethical concerns without fear of recrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share information and ideas; the company recognises right to work free from harassment; raise concerns about standards to managers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting incidents internally
rubrics_metrics.description: Report serious incidents involving harm or risk to staff, story/image problems, hoaxes or allegations of improper behaviour to supervisors and managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt internal reporting keeps senior officials informed and helps spot patterns and prevent wider problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life outside Reuters: avoid conflating personal and professional
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid confusion between professional activities and private interests or opinions; personal emails or statements that identify Reuters with a cause may breach Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use private email for potentially sensitive personal communications; do not use Reuters identity to obtain personal benefits; do not conduct private correspondence using company email or letterhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from bias: neutrality standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters requires freedom from bias; staff should be neutral, setting aside nationality and politics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to be scrupulously fair and balanced; give subjects opportunity to respond; monitor word choice to avoid implying bias (e.g., 'fears', 'insists', 'failed to comment').

rubrics_metrics.name: Take no side; tell all sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Never identify with any side in an issue, conflict or dispute; reflect all sides in text and visual stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectivity does not necessarily mean equal space for all sides; allocate space according to news judgement; always seek to know what you know and what you need to know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion and analysis separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a fundamental distinction between fact-based news stories and clearly labeled opinion pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not express opinions in news stories, voiced video or scripts; opinion must be labeled and carry disclaimers stating it does not represent Reuters' views; columns must present grounded views, not ungrounded provocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid discriminatory language and stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid inappropriate references to gender, ethnicity, religion, culture, appearance, age, and sexual orientation and be sensitive to unconscious stereotyping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neutral language; avoid gratuitous references to appearance; prefer plural professional group terms; be cautious with country stereotypes even when challenging them.

rubrics_metrics.name: No investment advice in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not express a personal view in reports on the merits of a particular investment; value judgments must be sourced to a named third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuters reports news and does not give investment advice; local laws may prohibit giving investment advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on Thomson Reuters: extra care
rubrics_metrics.description: Take extreme care to avoid any hint of bias when reporting on Thomson Reuters and its corporate affiliates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should be seen before publication by senior editors including the Global Editor for Ethics and Standards; include comment from a company spokesman (available in London, New York or Singapore); only pick up stories likely to be market moving or of significant general interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political and community activity restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters staff must not give support to any political party or group, nor identify Reuters with any one side in conflicts, and should avoid displays of political affiliation in the newsroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outside work staff retain rights (e.g., voting) but should avoid activities that create perception of bias; consult manager when in doubt; perceptions of conflict may require reassignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity in employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat employees fairly regardless of gender, ethnic, national or religious background, age, disability, marital or parental status, or sexual orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection for jobs, training and promotion should be based on skills and abilities and follow local laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity in the newsroom
rubrics_metrics.description: Embrace diversity of thought, style, experience, culture, race, gender identity and other characteristics in journalism and newsrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity enriches perspectives and leads to better journalism; welcome varying viewpoints in news decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media interviews and speaking engagements policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews or speaking engagements must be approved in advance by the journalist's manager and communications team and should not include personal opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must come from credible outlets; Reuters services take precedence; do not accept payment; if payment is inadvertent consult manager or Global Editor for Ethics and Standards; correspondents should confine remarks to reported Reuters material and not embarrass Reuters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conferences participation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in conferences and panels requires approval and must not undermine Reuters' reputation for integrity and independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists can moderate panels only if Reuters has editorial control over content; do not participate if panelists have paid to participate or are sponsor reps; avoid events primarily to sell a product; editors limited to one appearance a year at a company's conferences; reporters covering a company should not participate in that company's events; do not seek or accept payment for participation; approvals vary by sponsor and require escalation to named senior editors for company-sponsored events.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI and Generative AI: accountability and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Embrace generative AI opportunities while maintaining editorial accountability; be transparent about GenAI use and ensure accuracy, fairness and freedom from bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use generative AI to create or enhance any imagery for visual journalism; approved technologies may assist with non-altering tasks (e.g., describing a scene, generating shotlists/captions); never trust unverified facts from AI — independently verify and fact-check all AI-generated claims; avoid uploading Reuters/partner/third-party content to non-approved external tools; be mindful of LLM training biases; individual journalists remain fully accountable for AI-assisted work and should consult Ethics and Standards or Legal when in doubt.
